clue.text: City area blue collars won't fancy

indicators.note: to collar something is to grip it round the neck, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling down

indicators.note: as an adjective, fancy means elaborate or reworked, so the letters of won't are rearranged

explanation.surface: Manual workers are said to dislike some part of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collars' means grips round the neck, so the blue word encloses the rearranged letters from 'fancy', just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the central business district of a city is called its downtown, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Ruined party rally from the south

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means read upwards, so the word for the rally is reversed

parts.note: a demo, short for demonstration, is a protest rally

explanation.surface: A political party's march has been wrecked by people coming up from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the south' turns DEMO into OMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doomed is fated to fail, so it is as good as ruined.

clue.text: What's left with scrambled eggs missing yolk?

definitions.text: What's left with scrambled eggs missing yolk?
definitions.note: when eggs are made without their yellow centres, only the clear albumen parts remain

indicators.note: scrambled means jumbled, so the letters of the word with are rearranged
the yolk is the centre of an egg, so the middle letters of eggs are taken away

explanation.surface: A cook asks what remains when scrambled eggs are made without the yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' works on 'with', not on the eggs; 'missing yolk' strips the middle GG from EGGS. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear albumen surrounding the yolk is called the white, so eggs without their yellow leave only these.

clue.text: Change trains avoiding current model

indicators.note: avoiding means the letter standing for current is left out of trains

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone switches trains to avoid a model railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops I (current) from TRAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpose is to change the order or position of things, or move music into another key.

clue.text: Concert shone without New York diva

indicators.note: to concert is to arrange or bring together, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A New York singer gave a concert that sparkled while she was away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' is a verb, arrange, rather than a show. 'without' is part of the fodder, not an instruction to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: The American singer was one of the great pop and soul divas of the late twentieth century.

clue.text: Rise when about to finish

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
C is short for circa, Latin for about
to finish is to end

explanation.surface: Something goes up just as it is about to come to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to climb or go upward.

clue.text: A mystic originally found in south west India?

definitions.text: A mystic originally found in south west India?

indicators.note: found in means the preceding letters sit inside the surrounding ones

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of mystic is taken

explanation.surface: Is a mystic first to be seen in the south-west of India?
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts AM (A and the M from 'originally') between SW and I; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious teacher or holy man is given this title in India, so it is apt for a mystic.

clue.text: Medic sacked following record international outbreak

indicators.note: following means the rearranged letters come after the earlier pieces

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: sacked suggests something ransacked and thrown about, so the letters of medic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor is dismissed after an unprecedented worldwide spread of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' rearranges the medic; 'following' puts that after the record and international letters. 'record' looks like an adjective (record outbreak) but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A widespread outbreak of an infectious disease is an epidemic.

clue.text: Groom on time in equestrian event

parts.note: to groom someone is to dress them smartly
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A stable hand is on duty in time for a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' points to a stable hand; it means dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the competition in which horses are judged on precise trained movements.

clue.text: Order in church group covering comprehensive take on former state

indicators.note: in means the order's letters sit inside the church's

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
OM is the Order of Merit
full means complete or comprehensive
a circle is a group of people

explanation.surface: A church congregation is ordered to cover a broad view of a former regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' is only a link here: the pieces read in order. The Order of Merit is a British honour; the Church of England is the English state church.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to return to the starting point or original position after a sequence of changes.

clue.text: Payment to return fan mail regularly creating paperwork?

indicators.note: returning means the word for the payment is read backwards

parts.note: a giro is a payment by bank transfer, or a British benefit cheque

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of fan mail is taken

explanation.surface: Sending money back to answer a pile of letters from admirers sounds like a lot of administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns GIRO into ORIG; 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'fan mail'. 'Paperwork' is literal: work done in paper. GIRO is a British word for a bank payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful definition: the Japanese art of folding sheets is literally work with paper.

clue.text: Kind of glass work in beer barrels

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: barrels here is a verb: to barrel is to hold in a cask, so the beer word encloses the next piece

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A type of glass is produced inside beer casks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrels' is a verb here: ALE holds IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline is a milky, opal-like glass, so it is a type of glassware.

clue.text: Quits function abruptly before end of speeches

indicators.note: abruptly means cut off suddenly, so the last letter of the word for the occasion is dropped

parts.note: a function is a social event

indicators.note: end of means the final letter of speeches is taken

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a function suddenly before the speeches are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abruptly' cuts EVENT to EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means neither side owes the other anything, the same as being square or level.

clue.text: Sees end in desperate poverty

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild disorder, so the letters of sees end in are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone foresees ending up in desperate poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperate' looks like it qualifies 'poverty', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: neediness is the state of being in want, lacking money.

clue.text: Working out corporation structure

parts.note: a corporation is a body, as in a public body
a building is a structure

explanation.surface: Someone is figuring out how a company is organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working out' reads as figuring something out; it means exercise at the gym. 'Corporation' is also old slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out in the gym sense: bodybuilding is exercise to develop the muscles.

clue.text: Huge sale via thankful stores

definitions.note: an adjective here, defining a noun used attributively for something enormous

indicators.note: stores means the phrase sale via thankful holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: A grateful shop runs an enormous sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' looks like shops but is a verb: the words hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical sea monster gives its name to anything enormous, so it stands for something vast.

clue.text: Rich way for women to be cunning

indicators.note: for means one letter is swapped in place of another

parts.note: rich means wealthy
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A wealthy route for women to be clever.
explanation.walkthrough: In WEALTHY, ST (way) replaces W (women).
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means sly and furtive, so it is close to cunning or crafty.

clue.text: Curse of drivers inhaling endless methane supply

indicators.note: inhaling means the outer letters breathe in, and so contain, the rest

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation for drivers

indicators.note: supply as an adverb means supplely, flexibly, so the letters are bent into a new order
endless means the final letter of methane is dropped

explanation.surface: Motorists fear breathing in a never-ending stream of gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the gas's last letter, 'supply' (supplely) bends the rest into a new order, and 'inhaling' puts that inside the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal curse of excommunication, and so a curse in general.

clue.text: Attraction experienced by fair-headed romantics?

parts.note: attraction is a funfair ride, not love; fair-headed means heading for the fair, not blond, and couples ride it in the dark

explanation.surface: Blond lovers feel a pull towards each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attraction' wants to mean mutual desire and 'fair-headed' to mean blond; both are fairground senses. The answer is a dark boat or car ride through a tunnel, popular with courting couples.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair ride through a dark passage is an attraction that couples visiting the fair take together.

clue.text: Firm beginning to trade fur coats

indicators.note: coats is a verb: the fur word covers the next letter

parts.note: sable is a prized fur

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of trade is taken

explanation.surface: A company starting out in the business of fur coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coats' looks like a noun after 'fur' but is a verb: SABLE wraps T.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something firm is steady and not likely to shift.

clue.text: English right infiltrated by the same heartless journalist

indicators.note: infiltrated by means the following letters get inside the pair before
heartless means one of the central letters of ditto is removed

parts.note: ditto means the same again

explanation.surface: An English right-winger is infiltrated by a cruel copycat reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes one of the two middle Ts from the word meaning the same; 'infiltrated by' puts the result between the English and right letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior journalist who prepares and selects material for publication.

clue.text: Course that circuits a pit, namely around carts

definitions.note: singular in the clue, while the answer is the Italian plural for a set of starters

indicators.note: around means the concealed letters are turned the other way and read backwards
to cart is to carry, so the run of words circuits a pit namely carries the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A racetrack that loops round a pit lane, in other words a track for go-karts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carts' looks like go-karts on a circuit but is a verb, carries. Strictly the answer is plural, so 'Course' is a little loose: one starter would be antipasto.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian starter of cold meats, olives and vegetables is served as the opening dish of a meal.

clue.text: Press release flyer offering cruise

parts.note: PR stands for press release
an owl is a bird, a flyer

explanation.surface: A leaflet advertising a holiday at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' looks like a leaflet; it is a bird. 'cruise' means move slowly looking about, not a sea holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move about stealthily, as to cruise is to drive around slowly looking for something.

clue.text: Put on account to evade draconian tips

indicators.note: tips means the first letters of to, evade and draconian are taken

explanation.surface: Money is moved into an account to escape harsh rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' reaches back over three words: T, E, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on a show or a pretence is acting, so the past tense matches 'Put on'.

clue.text: Musical effect tool designed around band

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters are placed about the band's name
designed means put together in a new arrangement, so the letters of tool are reworked

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band

explanation.surface: A device for a musical effect is built round a group of players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the tool; 'around' puts that about the band, the American rock group R.E.M.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is a wavering repeated variation in pitch or volume, an effect used by singers and guitarists.

clue.text: Have sleeping partner perhaps in company practice?

parts.note: a habit is a regular practice

explanation.surface: A business arrangement where one partner takes no active part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeping partner' is a business term for an inactive investor; here it means someone you share a bed with.
explanation.definitionFit: Living together as a couple without marriage is what this verb means, so a bedfellow is one example.

clue.text: Character ending play getting prompt on a regular basis

indicators.note: the character ending a word is its final letter, here the last letter of play

parts.note: prompt can mean early or punctual

explanation.surface: An actor at the end of a play gets a cue on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' and 'prompt' both suggest the theatre; here they mean a letter and punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens once every twelve months recurs regularly, so it is an adverb of regular timing.

clue.text: Check vibrator over — it's a beast!

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

indicators.note: over means turned the other way, so the word for the vibrating part is reversed

parts.note: a reed is the strip that vibrates in a wind instrument

explanation.surface: An exclamation on examining a sex toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vibrator' is the reed of a clarinet or oboe; 'over' turns REED into DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas-time animal of the Arctic, the caribou, is a beast in the sense of any large animal.
